text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTainan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
Register(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTainan(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (RussianOfficial(x) ∧ CitizenshipTainan(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(CitizenshipTainan(Vladimir) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Vladimir)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
Register(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
Register(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Vladimir) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election or Vladimir is a manager at Gazprom.
